title: InLN: Knowledge-aware Incremental Leveling Network for Dynamic Advertising

problem.claim: Knowledge-aware dynamic advertising requires personalized ad delivery that models temporal changes in user preferences and product characteristics while using semantic knowledge from e-commerce knowledge graphs.

gap.claim: Existing methods do not comprehensively unify time-series user-product interactions with graph-structured knowledge triples, where interaction graphs change rapidly but knowledge graphs remain relatively stable.

contributions.claim: The work quantitatively defines the uneven distribution of temporal and semantic information in knowledge-aware dynamic advertising as temporal unevenness.

The Incremental Leveling Network (InLN) combines a periodic-focusing window for node-level dynamic modeling, a biased temporal walk for subgraph-level dynamic modeling, and an incremental leveling mechanism for knowledge-graph updating.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the three InLN techniques as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that InLN outperforms nine baseline models across three tasks.
The authors report a maximum improvement of 9.9% and an average improvement of 5.7%.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dynamic advertising needs accurate personalized delivery that accounts for temporal preference and product changes.
Knowledge graphs and graph neural networks are used to add semantic relatedness, improve accuracy, and support explanations.
Existing methods struggle to jointly model rapidly changing interactions and relatively stable knowledge-graph information.
InLN defines temporal unevenness and addresses it with three dynamic-modeling and knowledge-graph-updating techniques.
Experiments compare InLN with nine baselines across three tasks, with reported improvements up to 9.9% and averaging 5.7%.

source_observation.claim: The interaction graph changes rapidly while the knowledge graph remains relatively stable, producing uneven temporal and semantic information.

interpretation.claim: Dynamic systems that combine evolving interactions with stable semantic knowledge may require mechanisms that explicitly balance information across temporal scales.

application.claim: For comparable graph-based recommendation or advertising systems, model rapidly changing interactions and slower knowledge updates with separate but coordinated mechanisms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design generalizes beyond knowledge-aware dynamic advertising.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, task definitions, baseline identities, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, ablation results, statistical significance, or independent verification of the reported improvements.
